html:
A large brick complex in Rome, built in tiers against the slope of the Quirinal Hill around 100 to 110, as part of the building work for Trajan's Forum. It is usually credited to Apollodorus of Damascus, the architect of the emperor Trajan.

It is often called the world's oldest shopping mall. It had rows of small rooms opening onto streets and a vaulted hall on several floors. Many scholars now think most of the rooms were offices for the imperial administration rather than shops, though some trade surely went on there.

The building shows what Roman brick and concrete could do: curved facades, vaults and stairs packed onto a steep site. It survives far better than most of the forum around it, because it was later reused as a fortress and a convent. Today it holds the Museum of the Imperial Forums, a short walk from the Colosseum.
